en: Emptying stagnant water from old tires and cans stops Aedes mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever.
Washing an animal bite wound with soap and running water for fifteen minutes significantly reduces the risk of rabies.
Avoid swimming in floodwaters because rat urine carrying leptospirosis bacteria can enter your body through small skin cuts.
Eating any part of the common oleander plant can cause severe heart problems and requires immediate medical attention.
Washing your hands with soap after handling pet frogs prevents you from catching Salmonella bacteria that cause diarrhea.
Cooking pork thoroughly until there is no pink meat inside kills parasites that cause severe stomach and muscle pain.
The milky sap of the kalachuchi plant can cause severe skin rashes and eye irritation if accidentally touched.
Getting nine to eleven hours of sleep each night allows your brain to consolidate memories and repair growing tissues.
Applying sunscreen with at least SPF 30 protects your skin cells from ultraviolet rays that cause sunburns and DNA damage.
Eating orange fruits like Philippine mangoes provides vitamin A, which is essential for maintaining healthy vision and a strong immune system.
Washing your face twice daily with mild soap removes excess oil and prevents acne breakouts during early puberty.
Sweating cools your body down, but you must drink water to replace lost fluids and prevent dangerous dehydration.
